newsitem.title: MEXICO: Banco de Mexico net reserves slip, assets rise.
newsitem.headline: Banco de Mexico net reserves slip, assets rise.

text.p: Banco de Mexico said on Tuesday its international reserves as of May 16 were $21.727 billion, compared to $21.773 billion on May 9.
The central bank said that its net international assets as of the same date rose to $12.91 billion from $12.716 billion the week before.
The central bank said the increase of $194 million in net international assets during the period was due to:
--Net revenues from Pemex operations totalling $188 million
--Outflow due to net sales of foreign currency by the federal government totalling $125 million to cover servicing of external debt.

--A net gain of $131 million due to a combination of factors including changes in the dollar value of non-dollar assets and liabilities held by the bank; net returns on interest rates and from trading of metals and securities; and net deposits in dollar accounts from commercial banks at the central bank.
Banco de Mexico said that between May 9 and May 16 the monetary base rose 3.389 billion pesos due to an increase in demand for bills and coins.
In the same period, the government's balance at the central bank fell 9.472 billion pesos, mainly due to the periodic transfer of funds to federal entities and to extraordinary payments to teachers.

The bank said it undertook monetary regulation operations for a total of 5.163 billion pesos in order to neutralise an increase in liquidity that would have resulted in a decline in federal government deposits with its account at the Banco of Mexico.
The following tables detail Banco de Mexico's reserves and net domestic credit. All figures are in billions of pesos, unless otherwise indicated.
May 9 May 16
International Reserves
U.S. Dollars $21.773 bln $21.727 bln
Monetary Base 76.746 80.135
Net International Assets*
U.S. Dollars $12.716 bln $12.910 bln
Net Domestic Credit -23.744 -21.778
*Net International Assets are defined as gross international assets minus central bank liabilities with the IMF and assets of less than a six-month duration from other central banks.
